member.description: Optional property/method/signal/constant name to fetch just that member, e.g. 'size' or 'move_and_slide'.

localOperations.name: docs.feedback
localOperations.title: Feedback
localOperations.summary: Report how library entries worked out (worked, wrong, outdated, ...) so Summer can fix and re-rank them; fire-and-forget, opt-out honored.

entry_id.description: The library entry ID exactly as the loader printed it (kind/slug, optionally @content-hash). Never guess or reconstruct it.

outcome.description: worked = verified in-engine (playtest/screenshot passed). worked_with_fixes = worked after your changes (say what in deviation). wrong = incorrect content. outdated = no longer matches this engine version. incomplete = missing a needed case. did_not_apply = loaded but irrelevant to the task. misrouted = the description/metadata led you here wrongly.

note.description: Optional, max 280 chars. About the ENTRY only — never the user's project, files, or code.

deviation.description: Optional, max 280 chars. What you did instead of / on top of the entry's instructions.

reports.description: 1-10 outcome reports, batched at a natural checkpoint (one call, not one per entry).

engine_version.description: The Summer Engine version in use, e.g. "4.6.1".

agent_model.description: The model you are, e.g. claude-fable-5, gpt-5.5-codex; use "unknown" if unsure.

localOperations.name: docs.plan
localOperations.title: Plan
localOperations.summary: Plan the right Summer workflow for a game-building task: skill routes, tool groups, confirmation gates, and verification steps.

goal.description: The user's game-building goal or task.

assetPolicy.description: How aggressively to use paid asset generation.

verification.description: How much engine verification the agent should plan for.

localOperations.name: docs.read
localOperations.title: Read a Summer doc
localOperations.summary: Load one library entry by id — a skill's body and metadata, a tool's call recipe, a template's pin, a reference's text — ending in the feedback footer.

id.description: The entry id as returned by summer_search_library, <kind>/<slug>, e.g. skill/vfx-water-ripple or tool/screenshot. A file an entry links loads by <entry id>/<link as written>, e.g. skill/spatial-placement/references/kit-placement-tools.md; the linked files list at the end of a body gives each id.

part.description: skill = the body only (SKILL.md for skills, markdown body for references, how-to-call for tools, pin for templates); resource = the resource.yaml descriptor only; all (default) = both.

maxCharacters.description: Most characters of text to return (default 24000). A longer result is cut and says so.

localOperations.name: docs.search
localOperations.title: Search Summer docs
localOperations.summary: Search the Summer library by describing the task in plain words — ranked entries of every kind, with the id to load next via summer_read_library.

query.description: The task in plain words — what you are building, fixing, or looking for.

kinds.description: Restrict to these kinds. Omit for all kinds.

include_preview.description: Include status preview entries — not yet exercised in-engine by the Summer team (default true). false = stable only.

localOperations.name: engine.add_node
localOperations.title: Add a node
localOperations.summary: Add one node of any type to the scene at scenePath (it need not be the open tab) and save it. For 3 or more edits, write one engine.run_script instead. Next: engine.set_prop.

scenePath.description: Target scene path, e.g. 'res://main.tscn'

name.description: Name for the new node, e.g. 'Player', 'MainCamera'

localOperations.name: engine.align_distribute_3d
localOperations.title: Align or space 3D nodes
localOperations.summary: Align 2 to 16 3D nodes on one world axis (min, center, max) or space them equally (centers or gaps) from their visible bounds, then save the scene. One undo step.

scenePath.description: Exact target scene, e.g. 'res://levels/market.tscn'.

subjectPaths.description: Two to sixteen exact Node3D paths in the order to align or distribute.

axis.description: Finite, non-zero world axis [x,y,z]; normalization is automatic.

localOperations.name: engine.attach_to_surface
localOperations.title: Mount a piece on a surface
localOperations.summary: Turn a piece so its measured back faces a wall, ceiling or floor found by a ray, keep it upright and seat it at a standoff: pipes, lamps, signs. Saves the scene; a refused seat puts the piece back.

scenePath.description: Exact scene, e.g. 'res://levels/street.tscn'. It must be open; physics rays need it to be the active tab.

subject.description: Piece to mount (exact path from the scene root).

surface.description: Surface node. Without ray, the ray runs from the subject's origin to the nearest point of this node's bounds; with ray, hits on other nodes are skipped. The seat must land on this node (or inside it); a seat on any other node is refused and the piece is put back.

origin.description: Ray start [x, y, z] in scene space.

ray.description: Explicit ray that finds the surface plane and its normal. Pass this or surface (or both). With a ray only, a seat on another node is refused unless that node lies on the hit plane (a coplanar neighbour module, warned).

backAxis.description: The subject's LOCAL axis that faces into the surface. Measure it with summer_inspect_asset.

upAxis.description: The subject's LOCAL axis kept toward worldUp; not on the same line as backAxis.

worldUp.description: World direction the upAxis follows (projected onto the surface).

standoff.description: Gap between the subject's measured back face (the extreme of its visible bounds along backAxis) and the surface.

placeAt.description: current: the piece keeps its height and its place along the surface and only moves along the surface normal. hit: it also slides so the centre of its back face lands on the ray hit point (its height then follows the ray).

maxMove.description: Refuse, changing nothing, when the piece would end farther than this from where it starts. Place the piece near its mount first; raise this only for a deliberate long move.

maxDistance.description: Maximum ray length when looking for the surface.

collisionMask.description: Godot 3D physics layer mask for the ray.

localOperations.name: engine.batch
localOperations.title: Run engine ops in one call
localOperations.summary: Send a list of raw engine ops (AddNode, SetProp, RunVerification...) in one call: one undo step unless an op must travel alone, and one save at the end. Ask for receipt summary on long lists. For computed edits, engine.run_script is simpler.

scenePath.description: Required when ops contains scene mutations; exact res:// target scene path

ops.description: Array of operation objects, each with 'op' plus its parameters. InstantiateScene ops may also carry position, rotation_degrees, scale or transform; the tool sets them on the created node. Each InstantiateScene is its own engine request; the transforms of a run of them travel together before the next other op, so N placed pieces plus the save cost about N + 2 requests.

receipt.description: full (default): every engine receipt. summary: counts, failures with their op index, created node paths only (under 5 KB).

localOperations.name: engine.capture_gameplay
localOperations.title: Capture gameplay screenshots
localOperations.summary: Capture real gameplay frames (HUD included) from a hidden game window, no editor needed; game flags and player steps get past the title screen. Returns each frame's path and size: look at them before use.

project.description: Project folder with project.godot. Defaults to the MCP's bound project, then the working directory.

scene.description: Scene to start (res://... or uid://...). Default is the project's main scene, often a title menu; pass the gameplay scene for gameplay frames.

waitSeconds.description: Seconds the game runs before the first frame (default 3).

out.description: Output folder. Defaults to <project>/.summer/captures/<time>/ (ignored by git).

args.description: The game's own command-line flags, passed after "--" (OS.get_cmdline_user_args()), e.g. ["--autostart", "--solo"] to skip the title screen.

steps.description: What to do after waitSeconds, in order; exactly one of press, key, action, click, drag, wait, shot per step. Example: [{"press":"Play"},{"wait":3000},{"key":"Space"},{"shot":true},{"action":"jump"},{"wait":500},{"shot":true}]. With a shot step only shot steps save frames. A step that cannot run becomes a warning.

press.description: Press the visible button with this text (or node name); waits up to timeoutSeconds (default 10) for it.

key.description: Press a key by Godot name (Space, Enter, Escape, A, Up).

action.description: Press an input action from the project's InputMap, e.g. jump.

holdMs.description: How long key or action is held (default 100).

click.description: Left-click at [x, y] in frame pixels.

drag.description: Drag with the left button from [x, y] to [x, y] over ms (default 300).

localOperations.name: engine.clear_console
localOperations.title: Clear the editor console
localOperations.summary: Clear the editor's Output panel, for a clean slate before the game runs.

localOperations.name: engine.connect_ports
localOperations.title: Join two pieces at their ports
localOperations.summary: Move and turn one piece so its port (a Marker3D, or an open pipe end such as +Y) meets another piece's port: pipe to pipe, duct to duct. Refuses joins that tilt the piece. Saves the scene.

scenePath.description: Exact scene, e.g. 'res://levels/street.tscn'. It must be open in the editor (any tab).

subjectPort.description: An open-loop id from summer_inspect_asset, e.g. '+Y' (the outermost open loop facing +Y in the piece's own axes) or '+Y#2' (the next one facing +Y); or a Marker3D (or Node3D) name under the subject, whose -Z axis points out of the port; or an open-loop index. Ids and indices follow the stable order (facing, then position), never the radius.

targetPort.description: Port on the target (open-loop id such as '-Y', marker name, or open-loop index).

gap.description: Distance between the ports along the target port's direction.

rollDegrees.description: Extra turn of the subject, in degrees, about the joined port axis, applied after the ports are lined up. Axis: the target port's direction reversed, pointing from the joint into the target (receipt roll_axis). Sign: right-hand rule about that axis; positive turns counter-clockwise when you look back along the axis from inside the target toward the subject. Zero: the shortest turn that makes the subject's port face the target's from the subject's CURRENT orientation, so the same value gives different results from different start poses. Read other_ports in the receipt; once the ports are joined, a second call turns by exactly rollDegrees about the joint (180 flips a bend's free end to the other side).

maxTiltDegrees.description: Refuse the join, changing nothing, when it would tilt the subject's up axis (its local +Y) more than this many degrees from where it points now. Turning about the up axis is never tilt. The refusal names the predicted tilt and the subject ports that would join within the limit.

allowTilt.description: true joins even when the subject tilts more than maxTiltDegrees (a bend laid on its side, a sloped run). The receipt still reports tilt_degrees.

maxTriangles.description: Triangle budget (100-300000) per node when ports are open-loop ids or indices.

localOperations.name: engine.connect_signal
localOperations.title: Connect a signal
localOperations.summary: Connect a signal of one node to a method of another so the saved scene keeps it, verified from the saved .tscn. The receiver should define the method. Then test it with engine.play.

scenePath.description: Target scene path, e.g. 'res://main.tscn'

emitter.description: Node that fires the signal, e.g. './Player/HitArea'

receiver.description: Node with the handler script, e.g. './Player'

method.description: Method name in the receiver's script, e.g. '_on_hit_area_body_entered'

localOperations.name: engine.create_debug_report
localOperations.title: Write a debug report
localOperations.summary: Write a support-ready Markdown report: doctor checks, engine health, diagnostics, console and debugger output, and a hand-off prompt. No tokens or file contents; the person should still read it before sending it.

output_path.description: Where to write the Markdown report. Defaults to the open project root, or the current working directory if no project is open.

include_play_session.description: Launch the game briefly and collect post-play diagnostics.

play_wait_ms.description: Milliseconds to wait after launching the game when include_play_session is true.

max_console_lines.description: Console lines to include after filtering/deduping.

max_debugger_entries.description: Debugger error/warning entries to include after filtering/deduping.

include_doctor.description: Include summer doctor checks in the report.

localOperations.name: engine.create_scene
localOperations.title: Create a scene file
localOperations.summary: Create a new, minimal .tscn file with the root type you name. It fails when the file exists and never touches the open scene. Build it out with engine.run_script and that scenePath.

path.description: New scene path, e.g. 'res://scenes/empty_level.tscn'

rootName.description: Root node name for the new scene

rootType.description: Root node type. Default 'Node3D' (3D scenes); common alternatives: 'Node2D' (2D scenes), 'Control' (UI scenes), 'Node' (logic-only).

allow_temporary_scene_mutation.description: DEPRECATED, ignored. Scene creation no longer mutates any open scene; kept only so older callers don't break.

localOperations.name: engine.debug_views
localOperations.title: Render debug views of a pose
localOperations.summary: Render one pose as a grid of debug views next to the beauty pass: lighting only, albedo, world normals, overdraw and wireframe. Shows why a shot looks wrong.

scenePath.description: Scene to look at, e.g. "res://levels/town.tscn" (the SAVED file). Omit for the scene open in the editor.

bookmark_name.description: Pose from a camera bookmark (summer_camera_bookmark). Use INSTEAD of camera_position/camera_look_at.

camera_position.description: Explicit pose: camera position, "Vector3(x, y, z)". Goes with camera_look_at.

camera_look_at.description: Explicit pose: point the camera looks at, "Vector3(x, y, z)".

fov.description: Vertical field of view in degrees (1..179). Default: the bookmark's own, or 60.

views.description: Which views, in grid order (default all six: beauty, lighting, unshaded, normals, overdraw, wireframe).

update_previous.description: bookmark_name only: replace the bookmark's previous image (compare baseline) with this beauty tile. Default false: only a missing slot is created.

max_size.description: Longest edge of the returned JPEG in pixels (default 1536). Bigger costs more context; up to 4096 for detail work on a PC.

aspect.description: Frame width/height (default 1.7778 = 16:9). Every tile uses it.

save_to.description: Also write the returned image to res://.summer/shots/saved/<name>.jpg (1-64 of A-Z a-z 0-9 _ -; needs max_size <= 1024). Nothing is written without it, except one previous-image slot per rendered bookmark.

localOperations.name: engine.delete_camera_bookmark
localOperations.title: Delete a camera bookmark
localOperations.summary: Delete one saved camera viewpoint by name. Returns the names that remain.

name.description: Bookmark name for save/delete: 1-64 characters from A-Z a-z 0-9 _ - (e.g. "hero_closeup").

localOperations.name: engine.enable_plugin
localOperations.title: Enable an editor plugin
localOperations.summary: Enable an editor plugin in res://addons/<name>/ and return the real result: enabled with its autoloads, or why it failed. Older engines only queue it (queued true); then check engine.get_debugger_errors.

plugin.description: The plugin folder under res://addons/ (e.g. 'quest_tools') or its 'res://addons/<name>/plugin.cfg'

timeoutMs.description: How long the engine waits for the plugin to load (default 30000)

localOperations.name: engine.export_game
localOperations.title: Export the game
localOperations.summary: Export the game headless as the file the Summer Games store takes: a bundle for iPhone, Android, macOS and Windows, a web build or a desktop download. Returns path, sha256 and size. Upload it with store.upload_file.

project.description: Project folder with project.godot. Defaults to the MCP's bound project, then the working directory.

targets.description: Store platforms. Bundle: any of macos, windows, ios, android (omit to use every platform the project declares). Download: exactly one of web, macos, windows.

format.description: bundle (default): the summer.games store build. download: a web build or native download; the default when targets is ["web"].

timeoutSeconds.description: Stop the engine after this many seconds (default 900; a first export imports every asset).

alignDeclaration.description: A game with a server, set summer.build.json targetPlatforms to targets before exporting. The store refuses an upload whose declaration differs from the exported platforms (declaration_mismatch) and that spends the version.

localOperations.name: engine.export_templates
localOperations.title: List or install export templates
localOperations.summary: List or install Summer Engine export templates (web, macOS, Windows) from Summer's CDN, each sha256-checked. Needed only for engine.export_game with format download.

action.description: list: installed and published templates. install: download and install.

includeDebug.description: Also install the debug templates (for exports with debug true).

summerVersion.description: The installed Summer Engine version (Help > About, e.g. 0.7.1). Read automatically on macOS; needed on Windows and Linux.

localOperations.name: engine.fabricate_3d
localOperations.title: Make a mesh with Blender
localOperations.summary: Make a mesh with a bpy script in the person's own Blender (4.2 or newer, headless), import the .glb into the project and optionally place it. For exact modular kits and effect meshes, not characters or props.

source.description: Blender Python (bpy) code that creates mesh objects and leaves them linked in the scene. No export call — the engine exports the .glb. Pre-bound names bpy, bmesh, mathutils, math, Vector, Matrix, Euler.

name.description: Asset name — used for the default out_path (res://assets/fabricated/<name>.glb) and the instantiated node. Sanitized by the engine to [A-Za-z0-9_-].

out_path.description: Destination res:// path ending in .glb (default res://assets/fabricated/<name>.glb). An existing file is overwritten; '..' and hidden directories are refused.

target_size.description: Largest world-AABB dimension after instantiation — uniform scale, same rule as summer_instantiate_scene target_size. Only used together with import_to_scene.

import_to_scene.description: Instantiate the imported .glb into the currently open scene after import. Omit to only write and import the file.

parent.description: Parent node path in the open scene, e.g. '/' (scene root) or './World'.

position.description: Optional local position as the engine variant string 'Vector3(x, y, z)'.

max_seconds.description: Child budget in seconds (default 120, clamped 15-600) — Blender boot + script + procedural-colour bakes + export. The client waits max_seconds + 60 s.

checkpoint.description: Take a SummerGit checkpoint before the child runs (default false). The result confesses (no_rewind_point) when none could be taken.

blender_path.description: Explicit Blender executable. Only when the user named one; otherwise the engine resolves SUMMER_BLENDER_BIN, the editor setting filesystem/import/blender/blender_path, then PATH and well-known install locations.

localOperations.name: engine.frame_nodes
localOperations.title: Frame nodes and render them
localOperations.summary: Fit a camera to the world bounds of some nodes and render them with the scene's real environment and lights; bookmark_name also saves the pose. Returns the image and a caption with the pose and bounds.

scenePath.description: Scene to look at, e.g. "res://levels/town.tscn" (the SAVED file). Omit for the scene open in the editor.

nodes.description: Node paths relative to the scene root ("House1", "Props/Crate_02"). The camera fits their combined WORLD bounds (visible meshes, children included).

direction.description: Side the camera sits on: "front" (+Z), "back" (-Z), "left" (-X), "right" (+X), "top", "iso" (default, 3/4 from -X,+Y,-Z like summer_screenshot). Use from for anything else.

from.description: Explicit direction FROM the nodes TOWARD the camera, "Vector3(1, 0.4, 2)". Replaces direction. The fitted pose is checked in-engine: when walls block it, or it puts the camera behind or inside a one-sided surface (whose back is not drawn, so the image would look THROUGH it), the caption opens with a WARNING and offers the nearest valid from (+ fov); the requested view is still rendered.

fill.description: Share of the frame the nodes span along their limiting dimension (0.1..1.5, default 0.8).

fov.description: Vertical field of view in degrees (default 50).

max_size.description: Longest edge of the returned JPEG in pixels (default 1024). Bigger costs more context; up to 4096 for detail work on a PC.

aspect.description: Frame width/height (default 1.7778 = 16:9). Every tile uses it.

marks.description: Numbered Set-of-Mark labels over the largest visible nodes; the caption maps label -> node path (feed a label to summer_zoom mark). Each labelled node gets an occlusion test (centre + 4 bounds points); a node hidden behind other geometry is noted "(hidden behind <path>)" — ignore its label.

max_marks.description: marks only: cap on labels (engine default 32).

bookmark_name.description: Also save the fitted pose as this camera bookmark (1-64 of A-Z a-z 0-9 _ -), so later renders line up with it.

localOperations.name: engine.frame_shot
localOperations.title: Find camera poses for a shot
localOperations.summary: Find, score and save camera poses for a shot type (establishing, eye level, low angle, detail, corridor), tested against the real geometry. Returns the best 3 poses and a sheet, and saves the best as a bookmark.

scenePath.description: Scene to look at, e.g. "res://levels/town.tscn" (the SAVED file). Omit for the scene open in the editor.

shot.description: "establishing" (wide, whole subject, 12-40 deg up; a pose showing more than 15% empty ground or world edge ranks below every pose showing less), "eye_level" (player eye at spawn: its Camera3D kept inside 1.5-1.8 m, or eye_height, above the walkable surface under the camera), "low_angle" (hero, camera near the ground looking up), "detail" (close-up), "corridor" (down a lane/corridor inside the subject, found by a free-space scan, at eye height; prefers looking in from its open end). Eye-level and corridor cameras are never raised: a pose that cannot stand at eye height moves horizontally or is rejected. Every top pose states its camera height above the surface below it and its absolute y.

subject.description: Node paths to frame (required except for eye_level, where it is what the player looks at).

spawn.description: eye_level only: node the player stands at, e.g. the player or a spawn marker. Its own geometry never counts as an occluder.

eye_height.description: eye_level/corridor: exact camera height in metres above the walkable surface under the camera (default: 1.6; an eye_level spawn's own Camera3D keeps its height clamped into 1.5-1.8).

fov.description: Override the shot type's field of view (establishing 55, eye_level 60/75, low_angle 60 then widened, detail 40, corridor 60/75).

aspect.description: Frame width/height (default 1.7778 = 16:9). Every tile uses it.

hard.description: Path prefixes that must never block the view (walls, terrain): a pose they block is rejected.

soft.description: Path prefixes that may sit in front as framing (foliage, fences, props).

ignore.description: Path prefixes left out of the visibility pass entirely.

hard_layers.description: Physics layer mask: geometry whose nearest CollisionObject3D is on these layers is hard.

soft_layers.description: Physics layer mask for soft geometry.

occluders.description: Override the occluder classification. Default: path names (wall/house/terrain... = hard; tree/fence/lamp/prop/pipe... = soft), MultiMesh = soft, else size (<= 2.5 m = soft). The caption reports the counts by rule.

max_soft_fraction.description: Most of the subject that soft geometry may cover before a pose is rejected (0..1, default 0.67).

bookmark_name.description: Name for the saved best pose (default <shot>_<subject leaf>).

save_bookmark.description: Save the best pose as a camera bookmark (default true).

render.description: "sheet" (default): the top 3 in one labelled grid with real lighting; "best": the winner only; "none": scores only.

max_size.description: Longest edge of the returned JPEG in pixels (default 1536). Bigger costs more context; up to 4096 for detail work on a PC.

localOperations.name: engine.game_control
localOperations.title: Control the game clock
localOperations.summary: Pause or resume the RUNNING game, step exactly N frames, set the time scale, or list the live game instances. Step between two engine.game_probe reads for exact checks.

action.description: 'pause' suspends the game (Engine time frozen, physics inactive); 'resume' lifts the suspension; 'step' advances exactly N frames and leaves the game suspended; 'speed' sets the user time scale; 'instances' lists the live game instances (main + offscreen).

kind.description: action step — 'physics' (default, exact physics ticks) or 'process' (rendered frames).

speed.description: action speed — user time scale in (0, 100]. 0.25 = quarter speed, 2 = double.

instance.description: Game instance to address (default 'main'). Offscreen instances are named by summer_play with instance + mode offscreen; ignored by action instances.

localOperations.name: engine.game_input
localOperations.title: Send input to the running game
localOperations.summary: Drive the RUNNING game's input: a script of timed actions, keys and clicks, or record real input and replay it on a seeded instance. Input is an action: prove its effect with engine.game_probe.

action.description: 'script' schedules a timed sequence of synthetic inputs (SimulateInputScript); 'record_start'/'record_stop' capture the game's real input into res://.summer/replays/<id>.json; 'replay' plays a recording (or inline events) back.

events.description: action script (required) or replay (instead of recording) — up to 1000 timed events; last event within 36000 frames / 600 s.

at_frame.description: When to fire, in frames after scheduling (clock frame). Default 0 = the next frame.

at_ms.description: When to fire, in milliseconds after scheduling (clock ms); exact only on an instance with fixed_fps.

type.description: 'action' = InputMap action press/release; 'key' = keycode; 'mouse_click' = click at a position; 'axis' = analog strength between two actions; 'raw' = a recorded InputEvent replayed as {class, props}.

action.description: type action — InputMap action name (unknown_action if not bound).

pressed.description: type action|key — press (default true) or release.

strength.description: type action — press strength 0..1 (default 1). type axis — signed strength; negative selects action_negative.

hold_ms.description: type action|key — auto-release after this many ms (0 = stays pressed until a release event).

keycode.description: type key — Godot Key enum value (e.g. 32 = Space).

physical_keycode.description: type key — physical Key enum value (alternative to keycode).

position.description: type mouse_click — [x, y] in window pixels.

button.description: type mouse_click — MouseButton (1 = left, 2 = right, 3 = middle).

action_negative.description: type axis — action for negative strength (e.g. 'move_left').

action_positive.description: type axis — action for positive strength (e.g. 'move_right').

duration_ms.description: type axis — auto-release after this many ms.

class.description: type raw — InputEvent class to instantiate (e.g. 'InputEventKey').

props.description: type raw — properties set on the instantiated event.

clock.description: action script — whether at_frame ('frame', default, exact) or at_ms ('ms') schedules the events.

wait.description: action script|replay — wait for the last event to fire (default true; the engine caps a waited script at 20 s). Longer scripts use wait false and observe with summer_game_probe.

include_motion.description: action record_start — also record mouse/joypad motion events (default false; large).

save_as.description: action record_stop — res://.summer/replays/<name>.json to write instead of a generated id.

recording.description: action replay — the res://.summer/replays/<id>.json path returned by record_stop.

seed.description: action replay — assert the replay is reproducible; only accepted on an instance started with summer_play mode offscreen + deterministic true (else nondeterministic_instance).

instance.description: Game instance to address (default 'main'). Offscreen instances are named by summer_play with instance + mode offscreen; summer_game_control action 'instances' lists them.

localOperations.name: engine.game_probe
localOperations.title: Probe the running game
localOperations.summary: Read state and pixels of one frame of the RUNNING game together: the live tree, property values and a screenshot stamped with the same frame numbers. The evidence read of a playtest.

tree.description: Include the live scene tree ({name, class, path, children}) built game-side on the SAME frame as the pixels. Omit for no tree.

path.description: Subtree root, ABSOLUTE runtime path (default the scene tree root).

props.description: Up to 64 '<absolute path>:<property>' keys read on the same frame, e.g. '/root/Main/Player:position'. Values come back as Godot literal strings; misses land in missing.

screenshot.description: Capture the game viewport (default true). false = state only, cheaper and works when the window draws nothing.

max_dim.description: Longest image side in pixels, 16..4096 (default 1280); the frame is downscaled to fit.

instance.description: Game instance to address (default 'main'). Offscreen instances are named by summer_play with instance + mode offscreen; summer_game_control action 'instances' lists them.

localOperations.name: engine.get_console
localOperations.title: Read the editor console
localOperations.summary: Read recent editor Output messages, collapsed and filtered (errors and warnings by default; errors_only false for print output). A played game's runtime errors are not here: read engine.get_diagnostics first.

max_lines.description: Max lines to return after dedupe (default 100)

filter.description: Only return lines containing this string

type.description: Filter by message type at the engine level

errors_only.description: Drop info/std noise, keep errors and warnings (default true)

strict_errors.description: Drop warnings too — return errors only

raw.description: Bypass dedupe and level filtering — return engine output verbatim

maxCharacters.description: Most characters of text to return (default 4000). A longer result is cut and says so.

localOperations.name: engine.get_debugger_errors
localOperations.title: Read runtime errors
localOperations.summary: Read the played game's runtime errors from the debugger (null references, missing nodes, physics errors), collapsed, with call stacks on request. After a fix, read engine.get_diagnostics again.

max_errors.description: Max errors to return after dedupe

include_stack.description: Include stack traces for each error

include_warnings.description: Forward-compat flag — when engine supports it, returns warning bodies in the same call. Today the engine ignores it; use summer_get_debugger_warnings instead.

raw.description: Bypass dedupe — return engine output verbatim

maxCharacters.description: Most characters of text to return (default 4000). A longer result is cut and says so.

localOperations.name: engine.get_debugger_warnings
localOperations.title: Read runtime warnings
localOperations.summary: Read the played game's runtime warnings from the debugger, with file, line and call stack.

max_warnings.description: Max warnings to return after dedupe

maxCharacters.description: Most characters of text to return (default 4000). A longer result is cut and says so.

localOperations.name: engine.get_diagnostics
localOperations.title: Read errors and warnings
localOperations.summary: Read the editor console, the runtime debugger and script errors together, with complete counts and errors first. The first read after a change and after play. Next: engine.get_debugger_errors or engine.get_console for the details.

includeAll.description: Return the full engine diagnostics payload untrimmed (no severity reordering, no info-noise cap).

localOperations.name: engine.get_project_context
localOperations.title: Read the project context
localOperations.summary: Bind this session to the project open in Summer Engine and read it: project, current and main scene, engine health, project memory and warnings. Call it first in every chat; the scene tree and settings come on request (include). Next: engine.get_scene_tree.

include.description: Heavy blocks to add to the compact default: 'scene_tree' (the open scene's node tree, up to 200 nodes), 'capabilities' (the engine's full op/capability lists), 'settings' (project settings, curated groups). settingsPrefix/settingsPrefixes imply 'settings'.

settingsPrefix.description: Only return project settings whose key starts with this prefix, e.g. 'audio/' or 'application/config/'. Omit for the curated default set.

settingsPrefixes.description: Several settings groups at once, e.g. ['audio/', 'layer_names/2d_physics/', 'input/ui_']. Merged with settingsPrefix. Omit for the curated default set.

localOperations.name: engine.get_runtime_tree
localOperations.title: Read the running game's tree
localOperations.summary: Read the node tree of the RUNNING game: spawned enemies, autoloads and pooled nodes that editor reads never show. Needs a running game. Next: engine.inspect_runtime_node.

path.description: Subtree root to read, e.g. '/root/Main/Enemies'. Omit for the scene tree root.

maxCharacters.description: Most characters of text to return (default 4000). A longer result is cut and says so.

localOperations.name: engine.get_scene_tree
localOperations.title: Read a scene's node tree
localOperations.summary: Read the node tree of a scene: names, types and paths. Pass scenePath for an exact scene and depth for deep trees; the engine stops at depth 2 and 200 nodes by default and says truncated. Next: engine.inspect_node.

scenePath.description: Exact res:// scene path to inspect

depth.description: Maximum tree depth to walk. Engine default is 2 — pass a larger value for deep hierarchies.

limit.description: Maximum number of nodes to return. Engine default is 200.

maxCharacters.description: Most characters of text to return (default 8000). A longer result is cut and says so.

localOperations.name: engine.get_script_errors
localOperations.title: Check a script for errors
localOperations.summary: Check one GDScript file for parse and compile errors without running the game: line, message and severity of each. The first check after writing a script.

path.description: Script path, e.g. 'res://scripts/player.gd' or 'res://player_controller.gd'

localOperations.name: engine.grep
localOperations.title: Search project files
localOperations.summary: Search project files with a regular expression: file, line and text of each match, with optional context lines and a result cap. Then read the part you need with engine.read_file.

path.description: Search scope: a res:// directory or file, e.g. 'res://kit/' or 'res://kit/kit_manifest.json'. Default: the whole project.

glob.description: File filter passed to ripgrep --glob, e.g. '*.gd', '**/*.json', '!addons/**'. A glob also reaches files .gitignore would skip.

context_lines.description: Lines of context before and after each match (0-10, default 0).

max_results.description: Most matches to return (default 50, max 500). truncated:true means there were more.

max_line_chars.description: Clip every returned line to this many characters (default 240).

localOperations.name: engine.import_asset
localOperations.title: Find and import a Summer asset
localOperations.summary: Search the Summer asset library, import the best match into the project and, for a 3D model, add it to a scene. Needs the Summer sign-in. For an exact asset use engine.import_asset_by_id.

query.description: What to find, e.g. 'low-poly tree', 'wooden crate'

parent.description: Parent node path to add the asset under, e.g. './World'. If omitted, only imports (no scene placement)

scenePath.description: Required with parent. Exact res:// target scene path.

localOperations.name: engine.import_asset_by_id
localOperations.title: Import a Summer asset by id
localOperations.summary: Import one Summer asset by its id (from a search, the person's assets or a generation) into the project; a 3D model can go straight into the scene at scenePath. Needs the Summer sign-in.

path.description: Optional target res:// path. If omitted, a path is inferred from asset type and filename.

parent.description: Optional parent node path. For 3D models only; imports and instantiates under this node.

scenePath.description: Required with parent. Exact res:// scene that receives the 3D model.

name.description: Optional scene node name when parent is provided.

localOperations.name: engine.import_from_url
localOperations.title: Import a file from a URL
localOperations.summary: Download one file (model, texture, audio) from a URL into the project and run the import, so it is ready to use. For a model, next: engine.instantiate_scene.

path.description: Target path in project, e.g. 'res://assets/player.glb'. Auto-inferred from URL if omitted.

localOperations.name: engine.import_from_url_batch
localOperations.title: Import files from URLs
localOperations.summary: Download several files from URLs into the project in one call, with one import scan at the end.

path.description: Target path in project

localOperations.name: engine.import_hdri
localOperations.title: Import an HDRI sky
localOperations.summary: Find a CC0 HDRI sky on Poly Haven (or take an exact id) and import it into res://sky/ for environment light. Returns a ready engine.run_script snippet that wires it into the WorldEnvironment.

query.description: What kind of sky/environment, e.g. 'sunset beach', 'overcast field', 'studio'. Omit when assetId is given.

assetId.description: Exact Poly Haven asset id (lowercase slug, e.g. 'kloppenheim_02'). Skips the search.

resolution.description: HDRI resolution. 2k (default) is right for most games; 4k for hero skies; 1k for quick blockouts.

localOperations.name: engine.input_map_bind
localOperations.title: Bind input to an action
localOperations.summary: Create an input action when it is missing and bind keys or mouse buttons to it, for example jump to Space. Then try it with engine.play.

localOperations.name: engine.inspect_asset
localOperations.title: Measure a 3D asset file
localOperations.summary: Measure a 3D asset file without placing it: bounds, origin, meshes, largest flat faces, open pipe ends, Marker3D anchors and collision shapes. Measure each kit piece once before placing it. Next: engine.instantiate_scene.

path.description: Asset to measure, e.g. 'res://kit/facade/wall_single_01.tscn' (.tscn, .scn, .glb, .gltf, .res, .tres, .mesh or .obj). Loaded and instanced off-scene, never added to an open scene.

maxTriangles.description: Triangle budget (100-300000) for the face and open-loop analysis (AABBs and counts are always complete). summary.warnings says when the budget cut the analysis and which budget covers the whole mesh.

detail.description: summary: open_loops lists only port-like loops (radius over 2 cm with a partner loop facing another way, or the one opening of an end piece on its bounding-box face), or none. full: every open loop, including the outline of flat sheets. Every loop has a stable id ('+Y', '+Y#2') that summer_connect_ports accepts. Both start with the summary block (AABB, origin, the two largest opposite plane pairs with one_sided flags, port-like loop ids).

maxCharacters.description: Most characters of text to return (default 4000). A longer result is cut and says so.

localOperations.name: engine.inspect_node
localOperations.title: Read a node's properties
localOperations.summary: Read one node of the open scene: every editable property with its value and type, or only the fields you name (transform, global_transform, scene_file_path, aabb). Next: engine.set_prop.

path.description: Node path from scene tree, e.g. 'Player', 'World/Enemies/Boss', 'DirectionalLight3D'

fields.description: Only these fields: property names or globs (e.g. 'position', 'surface_material_override/*') and the derived fields transform, global_transform, scene_file_path, aabb, warnings. Omit for every property.

maxCharacters.description: Most characters of text to return (default 4000). A longer result is cut and says so.

localOperations.name: engine.inspect_resource
localOperations.title: Read a resource
localOperations.summary: Read a resource file (a mesh's bounds and surfaces, a scene's nodes, any resource's non-default properties) or a resource a node holds (nodePath and property). Next: engine.set_resource_property.

path.description: A resource FILE, e.g. 'res://materials/ground.tres', a mesh 'res://kit/meshes/wall_01.res', or a scene/model 'res://models/player.glb'. Loaded read-only in the editor. Do not combine with nodePath.

nodePath.description: With property, a node of the ACTIVE scene tab whose resource to read, e.g. 'Floor'.

property.description: With nodePath, the node property holding the resource, e.g. 'mesh', 'material_override', 'shape', 'environment'.

maxCharacters.description: Most characters of text to return (default 4000). A longer result is cut and says so.

localOperations.name: engine.inspect_runtime_node
localOperations.title: Read a node in the running game
localOperations.summary: Read the live properties of one node in the RUNNING game (transform, visibility, physics state...) without stopping it. Paths are absolute; take them from engine.get_runtime_tree.

path.description: Runtime node path, e.g. '/root/Main/Player'. Get it from summer_get_runtime_tree.

maxCharacters.description: Most characters of text to return (default 4000). A longer result is cut and says so.

localOperations.name: engine.instantiate_scene
localOperations.title: Add a scene or model as a node
localOperations.summary: Add an existing .tscn, .glb or .gltf as a child node in the scene at scenePath, placed in the same call (position, rotation_degrees, scale or transform). Pass target_size for imported models. Next: engine.screenshot.

scenePath.description: Target scene to receive the instance, e.g. 'res://main.tscn'

target_size.description: Normalize the instance's physical size - uniformly scale it so its largest world-AABB dimension equals this many units (chair 1.0, car 4.5, person 1.7). Strongly recommended for imported .glb/.gltf models. Older engine builds ignore it; the result then lacks scale_applied and carries a target_size_note.

position.description: Parent-local position [x, y, z], set right after the instance is created (on the node path its receipt reports).

rotation_degrees.description: Parent-local rotation in degrees [x, y, z].

scale.description: Local scale [x, y, z]. Not with target_size.

transform.description: Full local transform as "Transform3D(xx, xy, xz, yx, yy, yz, zx, zy, zz, ox, oy, oz)". Not with position, rotation_degrees, scale or target_size.

localOperations.name: engine.invoke_ui_action
localOperations.title: Run an editor action
localOperations.summary: Run one named editor action exactly as its menu item or shortcut would: open Project Settings, switch the main screen, toggle a panel. Editor work only; scene work is engine.run_script. Read the effect back with engine.ui_tree.

action_name.description: mode 'invoke' only (required there). The exact action name from a 'list' result — the stable shortcut path such as 'editor/project_settings', 'editor/save_scene', 'spatial_editor/focus_selection'. Palette-only commands are accepted too.

localOperations.name: engine.is_running
localOperations.title: Check whether the game runs
localOperations.summary: Check whether the game is running, and which scene it runs.

localOperations.name: engine.list_camera_bookmarks
localOperations.title: List camera bookmarks
localOperations.summary: List the camera viewpoints saved in this project: names, poses and dates. A bookmark gives screenshots that line up before and after a change: engine.screenshot with framing bookmark.

localOperations.name: engine.list_ui_actions
localOperations.title: List editor actions
localOperations.summary: List the editor's named actions (menu items and shortcuts) with labels and shortcuts, filtered by text. Actions marked denied are refused. Next: engine.invoke_ui_action.

filter.description: mode 'list' only. Case-insensitive substring over action name and label, e.g. 'project_settings', 'save', 'spatial_editor', 'bottom_panel'.

limit.description: mode 'list' only. Maximum actions returned (engine default 200, max 2000). The result carries total + truncated — never assume a capped list is complete.

localOperations.name: engine.measure
localOperations.title: Measure between nodes
localOperations.summary: Measure the gap or overlap on each axis between two placed nodes, or check that one face of many nodes lies on one plane. Finds facade gaps and modules that stand out. Changes nothing.

scenePath.description: Exact scene, e.g. 'res://levels/street.tscn'. It must be open in the editor (any tab).

mode.description: pair: gap or overlap per axis between nodes a and b. plane: whether one face of every node in nodes lies on one plane.

a.description: pair mode, first node (exact path from the scene root).

axis.description: pair mode, report only this axis.

nodes.description: plane mode, 2-32 nodes whose face is checked.

face.description: plane mode, which face, e.g. '+z' for the face pointing along +z.

space.description: world axes, or the axes of a (pair) / nodes[0] (plane) for rotated facades.

tolerance.description: Distance treated as touching (pair) or coplanar (plane). Default 5 mm.

localOperations.name: engine.navigation_probe
localOperations.title: Check a navigation route
localOperations.summary: Check whether two world points are connected on the scene's navigation map: readiness, snapped end points, route length and route points. ready false means no evidence, not no route.

scenePath.description: Exact 3D scene whose World3D navigation map should be queried.

navigationLayers.description: Godot navigation-layer bitmask; only enabled matching regions are used.

optimize.description: Use Godot's corridor-funnel path post-processing; false uses edge-centered points.

localOperations.name: engine.open_main_scene
localOperations.title: Open the main scene
localOperations.summary: Open the project's main scene (from project settings) in the editor, instead of guessing a scene file name.

localOperations.name: engine.open_scene
localOperations.title: Open a scene in the editor
localOperations.summary: Open a scene file in the editor and show its tab. A visible tab change for the person, not a target for edits: edits take scenePath. Take paths from engine.get_project_context; never guess them.

path.description: Scene path, e.g. 'res://main.tscn' or 'res://levels/level1.tscn'

localOperations.name: engine.place_adjacent
localOperations.title: Place a node against another
localOperations.summary: Move one node so its bounds face sits against another node's, lining up the other axes: modules edge to edge, storeys stacked. Saves the scene and verifies the gap.

scenePath.description: Exact scene, e.g. 'res://levels/street.tscn'. It must be open in the editor (any tab).

subject.description: Node to move (exact path from the scene root).

axis.description: Axis along which the two pieces meet.

side.description: max: subject on the reference's +axis side (its min face against the reference's max face). min: the -axis side.

gap.description: Distance between the two faces along axis. 0 = flush; negative = overlap.

alignOtherAxes.description: How to line up the other two axes: one mode for both, or per axis, e.g. {y: min, z: max} for same base height and one front plane.

space.description: world axes, or the reference's own axes for a rotated facade.

localOperations.name: engine.play
localOperations.title: Play the game
localOperations.summary: Start the game quietly (the editor keeps its tab and focus): the main scene or a given one, embedded or as a hidden offscreen instance, with an optional seed and fixed frame rate, or a local multiplayer session (players). Next: engine.is_running, then engine.get_diagnostics.

scene.description: Scene to run instead of main scene, e.g. 'res://levels/test_level.tscn'

instance.description: Name a game instance. 'main' (default) = the editor's embedded game. Any other name with mode 'offscreen' spawns a disposable parallel instance (at most 3) that the runtime tools address by this name.

mode.description: 'embedded' (default) plays in the editor; 'offscreen' spawns a hidden child process (requires instance != 'main').

deterministic.description: Offscreen only — launch with --fixed-fps 60 --summer-seed <seed> --audio-driver Dummy so the run is reproducible and input replays with seed are accepted.

seed.description: Pin the game's GLOBAL RNG for this launch (child gets --summer-seed <seed>; default 20260725 when deterministic:true and seed is omitted). Pins randi/randf/randi_range/randf_range/randfn, Array.shuffle/pick_random. Does NOT pin RandomNumberGenerator instances, scripts calling randomize(), or wall-clock reads. Omitted = randomized, as always.

fixed_fps.description: Fixed timestep for this launch (child gets --fixed-fps <n>): scene time decouples from the wall clock, the game runs as fast as it renders, frame-count-derived state repeats run to run, and at_ms input timing / GameStep frames map exactly. Opt-in per launch, never the default.

time_scale.description: Engine time scale for this launch (child gets --time-scale <f>). Not a determinism pin on its own.

speed.description: User time scale applied on session start, (0, 100] — e.g. 0.5 for half speed.

focus.description: Default false = QUIET play (PlayGame agent:true): the editor does not switch to the Game tab or grab focus for the embedded game, so the user keeps working. Pass true to launch the way the toolbar Play button does (Game tab + focus) — only when the user is watching and asked to see it. The result echoes agent_quiet:true when honoured; a launch result without it (posture_note) means the engine predates quiet play and most likely took focus.

players.description: Local Play for a Summer multiplayer game (engine with Local Play): start the game's authority headless plus this many clients on this machine, each joining through the game's own Summer.client.join. The scenes and queue come from the project's summer.build.json WorldDefinition; no account, Docker or game flags are needed. Omit it and pass queue to start the queue's minPlayers from summer.build.json; 0 forces one ordinary run. The result's local_play block lists every process and persona, plus warnings when the roster is outside the queue's minPlayers..maxPlayers.

spectators.description: Local Play: also start this many spectator clients (only with players).

queue.description: Local Play: the summer.build.json queue the local World stands in for (default: the first declared queue).

localOperations.name: engine.project_setting
localOperations.title: Set a project setting
localOperations.summary: Set one project.godot setting, such as application/run/main_scene, the window size, the renderer or the default gravity.

localOperations.name: engine.raycast
localOperations.title: Cast a ray in a scene
localOperations.summary: Cast one ray from any point in a scene: the node it hits, the point and the normal. Physics first, visible bounds as a declared fallback. Changes nothing.

scenePath.description: Exact scene, e.g. 'res://levels/street.tscn'. It must be open; physics needs it to be the active tab.

origin.description: Ray start [x, y, z] in scene (world) space.

direction.description: Ray direction [x, y, z], non-zero; normalized for you.

maxDistance.description: Maximum ray length in scene units.

collisionMask.description: Godot 3D physics layer mask for physics queries.

evidence.description: auto: physics first, visual AABB fallback when physics finds nothing (declared). physics or visual_aabb: that channel only.

localOperations.name: engine.read_file
localOperations.title: Read a project file
localOperations.summary: Read a text file of the project (res://), a line or byte window of it, or parts of a .json, with the whole file's sha256. Pass that sha256 to engine.write_file or engine.replace_text to change the file safely.

path.description: Project path, e.g. res://scripts/player.gd

max_bytes.description: Most bytes of content to return (UTF-8). Default 200000. A window or JSON selection is cut at this size too.

offset.description: Skip this many units (lines by default, see unit) before returning content. 0 = from the start.

limit.description: Return at most this many units (lines by default). The result's window.next_offset continues the read.

unit.description: What offset/limit count: 'lines' (default) or 'bytes' (cut on UTF-8 character boundaries).

json_path.description: For a JSON file: return only this value, e.g. 'pieces.wall_a', 'pieces["a b"]', 'items[3].size_m'.

keys.description: For a JSON object (the file root or the json_path value): keep only these keys; * and ? wildcards, e.g. ['wall_*'].

keys_only.description: For a JSON object: return only its key names (after the keys filter), not the values — a cheap table of contents.

localOperations.name: engine.recent_events
localOperations.title: Read recent engine events
localOperations.summary: Read the newest engine events (saves, plays, op results, script errors, imports) at once, and next_seq, the cursor to pass to engine.wait_for_event.

since.description: Deliver events with seq > since. Omit = the newest `limit` sequence numbers. 0 = the whole retained ring from the oldest (paged: pass next_seq back while truncated is true).

kinds.description: Event kinds to deliver (default: all). v1 kinds: op.applied, op.failed, script.error, play.started, play.stopped, scene.saved, scene.opened, import.completed, selection.changed, snapshot.published.

localOperations.name: engine.remove_node
localOperations.title: Remove a node
localOperations.summary: Remove a node and all its children from the scene at scenePath and save it. The root cannot be removed. One undo step. Remove top-level nodes only when the person asked for it.

scenePath.description: Target scene path, e.g. 'res://main.tscn'

path.description: Node path to remove, e.g. './World/OldEnemy'

localOperations.name: engine.repeat_along
localOperations.title: Repeat a scene along a line
localOperations.summary: Place copies of one scene along a line in one call: fence posts, clamps, a row of windows (at most 64). Returns the created node paths and saves the scene once.

scenePath.description: Exact scene, e.g. 'res://levels/street.tscn'.

template.description: Scene to instance for every copy (.tscn, .scn, .glb, .gltf).

parent.description: Parent for the copies; start/end/direction are in this parent's local space.

end.description: Line end. With spacing as many copies as fit; with count, count copies from start to end.

direction.description: Instead of end, the row direction; needs count and spacing.

align.description: With end + spacing, where the leftover length goes.

namePrefix.description: Copies are named <namePrefix>_<n> (default the template file name).

localOperations.name: engine.replace_node
localOperations.title: Replace a node
localOperations.summary: Replace a node with another scene or node type, keeping its parent, index, name, transform and children; the saved file is read back to prove it. Next: engine.get_scene_tree.

scenePath.description: Target scene path, e.g. 'res://main.tscn'

path.description: Node path to replace, e.g. './House3/Front/G_f2_door'

type.description: New node type, e.g. 'RigidBody3D'. Give exactly one of type or scene.

scene.description: Scene or model to replace with, e.g. 'res://kit/wall_door_02.tscn'. Give exactly one of type or scene.

localOperations.name: engine.replace_text
localOperations.title: Replace text in a project file
localOperations.summary: Replace text in an existing project file. The text must match exactly once unless replace_all is set; the write is guarded by the file's sha256. Then check scripts with engine.get_script_errors.

path.description: Project path, e.g. res://scripts/player.gd

replace_all.description: Replace every exact occurrence instead of requiring one unique match.

localOperations.name: engine.run_editor_script
localOperations.title: Run a script in a headless editor
localOperations.summary: Run an EditorScript func _run() in a fresh headless editor against the project on disk: batch and project-wide jobs such as re-saving many scenes. It cannot see unsaved edits. For the open scene use engine.run_script.

source.description: EditorScript GDScript source with `func _run():`. '@tool' / 'extends EditorScript' are optional — missing lines are prepended and reported in normalizations.

max_seconds.description: Time budget in seconds for the child editor (default 120, clamped 15-600). Include boot time — large projects can take 30s+ just to start.

checkpoint.description: Take a SummerGit checkpoint before the child editor runs. The result confesses (no_rewind_point) when none could be taken.

localOperations.name: engine.run_script
localOperations.title: Run a script on a scene
localOperations.summary: Run one GDScript func run(ctx) in the live editor on the scene at scenePath: the way to make 3 or more scene edits, loops, grids and procedural meshes. Returns reports, output and errors. Loop: engine.world_snapshot, this, engine.snapshot_diff, engine.screenshot.

scenePath.description: The scene to run against, e.g. 'res://main.tscn'. Opened first when it is not the edited scene, then the person's tab is restored. Omit only to run against whatever scene is open.

source.description: GDScript source containing `func run(ctx):`. No extends/@tool line — just the function (plus any helpers).

max_seconds.description: Time budget in seconds (default 20, clamped 5-120). The script blocks the editor while it runs — keep it short.

checkpoint.description: Take a SummerGit checkpoint before running (default true). The result confesses (no_rewind_point) when no checkpoint could be taken.

undo.description: Transaction mode (newer engines). 'action' (engine default) makes the run one undo action and rolls back on a runtime error; 'none' is checkpoint only. Older engines ignore this.

localOperations.name: engine.runtime_animate
localOperations.title: Drive animation in the running game
localOperations.summary: Read and drive animation in the RUNNING game: AnimationPlayer clips, AnimationTree states and Skeleton3D bone poses. cmd state only reads. Prove motion with two reads around engine.game_control step.

target.description: 'player' = AnimationPlayer (RuntimeAnimation), 'tree' = AnimationTree state machine (RuntimeAnimationTree), 'bones' = Skeleton3D poses (GetRuntimeBones).

path.description: ABSOLUTE runtime path of the AnimationPlayer / AnimationTree / Skeleton3D.

cmd.description: Default 'state' (read-only). target player: state|play|pause|stop|seek|speed. target tree: state|travel|start|stop|set_param|get_param. Ignored for target bones.

name.description: target player play — clip name (unknown_animation lists the clips).

position.description: target player seek — position in seconds.

speed.description: target player speed — speed_scale (1.0 = normal, negative plays backwards).

from_end.description: target player play — start from the end (backwards).

blend.description: target player play — custom blend time in seconds.

update.description: target player seek — apply the pose immediately (default true).

state.description: target tree travel/start — state machine node name (unknown_state lists them).

reset.description: target tree travel/start — reset the destination clip (default true).

param.description: target tree set_param/get_param — parameter path, e.g. 'parameters/Blend/blend_amount'.

value.description: target tree set_param — new value (JSON scalar or Godot literal string).

playback_path.description: target tree — state machine playback parameter (default 'parameters/playback'; nested machines use 'parameters/<Node>/playback').

bones.description: target bones — bone names to read (omit for the first 256; page larger rigs with this filter).

include_rest.description: target bones — also return each bone's rest Transform3D.

instance.description: Game instance to address (default 'main'). Offscreen instances are named by summer_play with instance + mode offscreen; summer_game_control action 'instances' lists them.

localOperations.name: engine.runtime_call
localOperations.title: Call a method in the running game
localOperations.summary: Call one method on a node in the RUNNING game and return its result, to trigger gameplay code directly. A call is an action, not proof: check what it did with engine.game_probe.

path.description: ABSOLUTE runtime node path, e.g. '/root/Main/Player'.

method.description: Method name to call on the node, e.g. 'take_damage', 'get_velocity'.

args.description: Positional arguments. JSON scalars, arrays and objects pass as-is; math values as Godot literal strings ('Vector3(0, 1, 0)'). Object and RID arguments are refused (bad_args).

instance.description: Game instance to address (default 'main'). Offscreen instances are named by summer_play with instance + mode offscreen; summer_game_control action 'instances' lists them.

localOperations.name: engine.runtime_set
localOperations.title: Set a property in the running game
localOperations.summary: Set one property on a node in the RUNNING game (the live object, never the scene file) and read back whether it applied: move the player, set health, flip a flag. Then check with engine.game_probe.

path.description: ABSOLUTE runtime node path, e.g. '/root/Main/Player' (from summer_game_probe tree).

property.description: Property name, e.g. 'position', 'health', 'visible'. 'script' and 'owner' are refused.

value.description: New value. JSON scalars for primitives; Godot literal strings for math types ('Vector3(1, 2, 3)', 'Color(1, 0, 0, 1)'). Compared with Variant equality, so 1 and 1.0 both count as applied.

field.description: Optional sub-field to set instead of the whole value, e.g. 'x' on a Vector3 property.

instance.description: Game instance to address (default 'main'). Offscreen instances are named by summer_play with instance + mode offscreen; summer_game_control action 'instances' lists them.

localOperations.name: engine.runtime_spawn
localOperations.title: Spawn or free in the running game
localOperations.summary: Spawn a scene into the RUNNING game (action spawn) or free a live node (action free) to set up a test. The scene file is not touched. Then check with engine.game_probe.

action.description: 'spawn' instantiates a PackedScene under parent (SpawnRuntimeScene); 'free' removes a node (FreeRuntimeNode).

parent.description: action spawn — ABSOLUTE runtime path of the parent, e.g. '/root/Main/Enemies'.

scene.description: action spawn — PackedScene to instantiate, e.g. 'res://enemies/goblin.tscn'.

name.description: action spawn — node name; the engine renames on collision and reports renamed_to.

props.description: action spawn — properties set on the new node before it enters the tree ({position 'Vector3(0, 1, 0)', health 50}). Unknown ones land in prop_warnings, never fail the spawn.

path.description: action free — ABSOLUTE runtime path of the node to free.

mode.description: action free — 'queue_free' (default, frees at the end of the frame) or 'free' (immediate).

instance.description: Game instance to address (default 'main'). Offscreen instances are named by summer_play with instance + mode offscreen; summer_game_control action 'instances' lists them.

localOperations.name: engine.save_camera_bookmark
localOperations.title: Save a camera bookmark
localOperations.summary: Save a named camera viewpoint in the project (res://.summer/camera_bookmarks.json): position and look_at as Vector3 literals, or neither to take the editor's 3D camera. The scene file is not touched. Next: engine.screenshot.

name.description: Bookmark name for save/delete: 1-64 characters from A-Z a-z 0-9 _ - (e.g. "hero_closeup").

position.description: save only. Camera position as a Godot literal, e.g. "Vector3(0, 5, 12)". Goes together with look_at; omit BOTH to capture the current editor 3D viewport camera.

look_at.description: save only. Point the camera looks at, e.g. "Vector3(0, 1, 0)". Must differ from position.

fov.description: save only. Vertical field of view in degrees (1..179, default 60). With a captured viewport pose the viewport camera's fov wins.

localOperations.name: engine.save_scene
localOperations.title: Save a scene
localOperations.summary: Save the scene at scenePath, or save it under a new path. Scene edits already save once; use this for a standalone save or a save-as.

scenePath.description: Scene to save, e.g. 'res://main.tscn'

path.description: Optional save-as path, e.g. 'res://levels/level2.tscn'

localOperations.name: engine.scene_audit
localOperations.title: Audit a 3D scene
localOperations.summary: Check a saved 3D scene for visual and placement problems: holes, exposed edges, floor gaps, floating or sunken props, overlaps, z-fighting, light limits. Returns issues by severity, each with the next tool. Changes nothing.

scenePath.description: Scene to audit, e.g. "res://levels/town.tscn" (the SAVED file). Omit for the scene open in the editor.

checks.description: Only these checks (default all 15). Fewer checks run faster (duplicate, lights, transform and resource need no physics); rerun a check budget_ms left partial on its own.

root.description: Report only issues under this node (subtree), e.g. "Block3". The whole scene is still loaded, so walls and floors outside it count as surroundings.

min_severity.description: "error" (only errors), "warn" (errors and warnings) or "look" (default: everything, including look items that only ask you to look).

offset.description: Skip this many issues of the sorted, filtered list (paging; the result names the next offset).

limit.description: Issues per page (default 15, max 50). The result is capped at 5 KB; a page that does not fit is cut and says so.

budget_ms.description: Editor time for the whole audit (default 3000 ms). Each check gets a share weighted by its usual cost (unused time passes on); a check past its share stops and counts.<check>.partial gives the share it covered. Under load, rerun the partial checks with checks or a larger budget.

key.description: The issue's key from a previous result (issues[].key).

reason.description: Why it is fine, e.g. "coplanar faces hidden behind a sign".

accept.description: Accept look or warn items you judged fine (up to 50 per call): [{key, reason}] with keys from this scene's issues. Written to res://.summer/audit-accept.json (the only file the audit writes), then counted (counts.<check>.accepted) but hidden on every later audit until their evidence changes materially (severity rises, or the measured size moves by over 25%): then they show again with accept_stale. Errors cannot be accepted.

show_accepted.description: List accepted items too (each with its accepted reason). Default false: hidden, only counted.

render.description: "sheet": also return ONE inline image of the first 6 issues of this page framed up close from their open side, each tile labelled with its issue number. Default "none".

localOperations.name: engine.screenshot
localOperations.title: Take a screenshot
localOperations.summary: Return a frame as an image you see: the editor viewport, an offscreen render of a scene (preset, camera, bookmark or free pose, numbered marks) or the running game. A blank viewport frame means no redraw yet: capture again.

target.description: "viewport" = editor current view (default), "scene" = offscreen render of a scene file, "game" = running game frame

scenePath.description: target:"scene" only. Full scene path, e.g. "res://main.tscn". Omit to render the currently-open scene.

framing.description: target:"scene" only, 3D scenes. Camera direction preset: "iso" = 3/4 diagonal view, "top" = straight down, "front" = camera at +Z, "back" = camera at -Z, "left" = camera at -X, "right" = camera at +X. "auto" (default) is an alias of "iso". "camera" = render through the scene's OWN Camera3D with its REAL WorldEnvironment - the only edit-time framing that truthfully shows lighting/mood. "bookmark" (+ bookmark_name) = the fixed pose saved with summer_camera_bookmark; "free" (+ camera_position, camera_look_at, fov) = an explicit fixed pose. Both keep the REAL WorldEnvironment and repeat exactly, so before/after frames line up. The result reports the resolved framing - an older engine echoes a preset instead, and the caption warns.

bookmark_name.description: framing:"bookmark" only (implies it when framing is omitted). Name of a bookmark saved with summer_camera_bookmark (list them with action:"list"). Fails with failure_reason "unknown_bookmark" (+ the available names) when it does not exist.

size.description: target:"scene" only. Output image [width, height] in pixels.

nodePath.description: target:"scene" only. Node path relative to the scene root (e.g. "Player/Mesh") to frame INSTEAD of the whole scene — the camera fits that node's combined bounds (3D visual AABBs or 2D rects, children included). A bare unique name is also found recursively. Fails with failure_reason "node_not_found" when the path does not resolve (no silent whole-scene fallback). Cannot combine with a fixed pose (framing "camera"/"free"/"bookmark").

camera_path.description: framing:"camera" only. Path of the Camera3D to render through (relative to the scene root) when the scene has several cameras or none marked current. Omit to use the scene's current/first Camera3D.

camera_position.description: framing:"free" only (implies it when framing is omitted). Camera position as a Godot literal, e.g. "Vector3(0, 5, 12)". Goes together with camera_look_at.

camera_look_at.description: framing:"free" only. Point the camera looks at, e.g. "Vector3(0, 1, 0)". Must differ from camera_position.

fov.description: framing:"free" / "bookmark" only. Vertical field of view in degrees (1..179; default 60 for "free", the bookmark's own for "bookmark").

marks.description: target:"scene" only, 3D scenes. Draw a Set-of-Mark overlay - numbered tags + box outlines over the largest visible VisualInstance3D nodes (lights excluded), ranked by projected screen area. The caption lists label -> node path (scene-root-relative) so you can name what you see, and an occlusion test (centre + 4 bounds points from the rendered camera) notes "(hidden behind <path>)" on labels whose node is hidden - ignore those. Works with every framing. 2D scenes return marks_unsupported. Default false.

max_marks.description: marks:true only. Cap on numbered labels (engine default 32, at most 128). The caption says when the cap truncated the list.

compare_previous.description: framing:"bookmark" only. Return ONE image of [previous render | now | difference map] for the bookmark, with the share of changed pixels (summer_shot_sheet compare_previous with this one bookmark); this render then replaces the bookmark's previous image in res://.summer/shots/<bookmark>.jpg. A plain bookmark render (no marks, at most 1024 px) only creates that image when it is missing and never overwrites the compare baseline.

update_previous.description: framing:"bookmark" only. Replace the bookmark's previous image (its compare baseline) with this clean render. Default false: an existing baseline is kept.

localOperations.name: engine.select_node
localOperations.title: Select a node in the editor
localOperations.summary: Select a node in the editor's scene tree and show it in the inspector, so the person sees it. The scene does not change.

scenePath.description: Open this scene first, then select the node

localOperations.name: engine.set_prop
localOperations.title: Set a node property
localOperations.summary: Set one property of a node in the scene at scenePath and save it. Values use Godot syntax: "Vector3(0, 1, 0)", "Color(1, 0, 0, 1)", or a resource class such as "BoxMesh". For 3 or more edits, write one engine.run_script.

scenePath.description: Target scene path, e.g. 'res://main.tscn'

path.description: Node path, e.g. './World/Player'

value.description: Value in Summer Engine variant-string format for complex types, native JSON for primitives

localOperations.name: engine.set_resource_property
localOperations.title: Set a property of a node's resource
localOperations.summary: Set a property inside a resource a node holds, such as a collision shape's size or a material's albedo_color, and save the scene. The resource must exist first: assign it with engine.set_prop.

scenePath.description: Target scene path, e.g. 'res://main.tscn'

resourceProperty.description: Resource property on the node, e.g. 'shape', 'mesh', 'material_override'

value.description: Value in Summer Engine variant-string format

localOperations.name: engine.shot_sheet
localOperations.title: Render a sheet of views
localOperations.summary: Render several bookmarks or poses into one labelled grid with real lighting, and compare each bookmark with its last render (difference map). The quick look at every hero view after a change.

scenePath.description: Scene to look at, e.g. "res://levels/town.tscn" (the SAVED file). Omit for the scene open in the editor.

bookmark_name.description: Pose from a camera bookmark (summer_camera_bookmark). Use INSTEAD of camera_position/camera_look_at.

camera_position.description: Explicit pose: camera position, "Vector3(x, y, z)". Goes with camera_look_at.

camera_look_at.description: Explicit pose: point the camera looks at, "Vector3(x, y, z)".

fov.description: Vertical field of view in degrees (1..179). Default: the bookmark's own, or 60.

label.description: Tile label (1-64 printable characters, no quotes, backslashes or $). Default: the bookmark name or 'shot N'.

shots.description: 1-12 shots, each a bookmark_name OR camera_position + camera_look_at (+ fov), with an optional label. Rendered in this order, left to right, top to bottom.

view.description: "beauty" (default: real environment, lights, fog, tonemap), "lighting" (light only), "unshaded" (albedo/texture only), "normals" (world normals, x red y green z blue), "overdraw", "wireframe".

compare_previous.description: For bookmark shots: one row per bookmark of [previous render | now | difference map], with the share of changed pixels in the caption. The previous render is the bookmark's slot in res://.summer/shots/; this render replaces it (it is the next baseline).

update_previous.description: Replace each bookmark's previous image (its compare baseline) with this render without comparing. Default false: a sheet without compare_previous only creates a missing slot and never overwrites an existing baseline.

max_size.description: Longest edge of the returned JPEG in pixels (default 1536). Bigger costs more context; up to 4096 for detail work on a PC.

aspect.description: Frame width/height (default 1.7778 = 16:9). Every tile uses it.

save_to.description: Also write the returned image to res://.summer/shots/saved/<name>.jpg (1-64 of A-Z a-z 0-9 _ -; needs max_size <= 1024). Nothing is written without it, except one previous-image slot per rendered bookmark (created when missing; replaced only by compare_previous or update_previous).

localOperations.name: engine.snap_to_surface
localOperations.title: Snap a node onto a surface
localOperations.summary: Move one 3D node along a ray until it sits at the given gap on the first surface (floor, ramp, shelf, table), then save the scene. Returns before and after transforms and the evidence.

scenePath.description: Exact scene containing the subject, e.g. 'res://levels/market.tscn'.

subjectPath.description: Exact Node3D path relative to the scene root, e.g. './Props/Crate'.

direction.description: Finite world-space cast direction [x,y,z] whose squared length exceeds 0.00001. Defaults downward.

maxDistance.description: Maximum cast and overlap-recovery distance in scene units.

gap.description: Requested separation from the support surface; must not exceed maxDistance.

alignUp.description: Rotate the subject's current world up toward an exact physics contact normal before seating it.

localOperations.name: engine.snapshot_diff
localOperations.title: Compare two scene snapshots
localOperations.summary: Compare two scene snapshots: added, removed and changed nodes and count changes. The proof that a change did what you meant; an empty diff after a change means it did not land. Next: engine.screenshot.

from_id.description: snapshot_id of the BEFORE snapshot (from summer_world_snapshot).

to_id.description: snapshot_id of the AFTER snapshot. Omit to snapshot the current state now and diff against that.

localOperations.name: engine.starcast
localOperations.title: Read the space around a node
localOperations.summary: Read the clearance around one 3D node in 26 directions: what blocks each side and how far, contact, grounding and nearby objects. Changes nothing. Use it before and after placing.

scenePath.description: Exact scene containing the subject, e.g. 'res://levels/level1.tscn'.

path.description: Exact Node3D path relative to the scene root, e.g. './World/Crate'.

detail.description: summary: compact placement report (at most 5 KB). full: adds bounded hit geometry, an objects table, and nearby lists (at most 12 KB; the engine downgrades to summary rather than exceed it).

maxDistance.description: Maximum outward cast distance in scene units.

nearbyRadius.description: Maximum gap from the subject bounds for the nearby-object lists (full detail).

directionSpace.description: Cast along world axes, or along the subject's orthonormalized local axes for rotated subjects.

collisionMask.description: Godot 3D physics layer mask queried by rays, shape contacts/overlaps, and nearby-collider scans.

collideWithAreas.description: Include Area3D objects as well as physics bodies.

maxHitsPerDirection.description: Maximum physics hits and visual AABB hits retained for each direction.

maxResults.description: Maximum retained contact/overlap and nearby entries per evidence channel.
